llm.summary: The skill matches its Kia vehicle-control purpose, but it asks for plaintext Kia credentials and keeps a long-lived vehicle session, so it needs careful review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The setup example places KIA_USERNAME and KIA_PASSWORD in project or user MCP JSON, exposing credentials for an account that can reveal vehicle location and control vehicle functions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup runs the disclosed npm package via npx -y kiaaccess-mcp from MCP config; the artifact contains no executable code itself, but the package is unpinned and executes remotely supplied npm code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions require explicit confirmation for write commands, provide dry-run behavior without confirm:true, say not to guess vehicle keys, and separate write exposure by KIA_WRITE_MODE.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact says a remember-me token is stored locally and refreshes sessions silently forever, and an export tool can return the refresh token in plaintext as a full MFA bypass, even though both are disclosed and there is a forget-session tool.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to read Kia vehicle status/location and send Kia commands; the listed tools directly match that purpose, including high-impact climate, charging, lock, and unlock actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the MCP server access to your Kia account and vehicle controls. Prefer KIA_WRITE_MODE=none unless you need commands, avoid project configs that may be committed, restrict config file permissions, and treat any exported refresh token like a password because it bypasses MFA.
llm.findings: [AS2] expected: The artifact does instruct users to put Kia credentials in MCP configuration; account credentials are expected for this integration, but plaintext storage is a real concern because the same account grants vehicle location and command access.
